sources.title: Refrigerator & Freezer - Sealed System Operation
sources.notes: Describes compressor, condenser, capillary tube, evaporator, and where condenser heat is rejected.

sources.title: 4.3 Refrigerators and Heat Pumps - University Physics Volume 2
sources.notes: Explains that a refrigerator removes heat from the cold reservoir, requires work input, and rejects heat to the outside at the condenser.

sources.title: Vì sao tủ lạnh Samsung nóng hai bên cạnh tủ?
sources.notes: Explains that some refrigerator designs dissipate heat through pipes integrated into the side walls.

findings.summary: A refrigerator removes heat from the cooled interior and rejects that heat to the warmer surroundings; the cycle requires work input.
In a household refrigeration system, refrigerant absorbs heat at the evaporator, is compressed, and then rejects heat at the condenser.
GE notes that condenser heat may be discharged from the front or rear depending on refrigerator/freezer design.
findings.notes: Prevents overgeneralizing rear heating to every model.

findings.summary: Samsung documents designs where heat-dissipation piping is integrated into the side walls, causing the sides to become warm during operation.
findings.notes: Useful design variation for continuity-safe explanation.

findings.summary: Exterior warmth at the designed heat-rejection area can be a normal consequence of the refrigeration process.
findings.notes: Should not be generalized to every abnormal overheating symptom.

uncertainties.description: The exact location and temperature of the heat-rejection surface depend on refrigerator model and installation, so the video must avoid claiming that every unit becomes hot specifically at the rear.
